> 🌱 STARBiE — Smart Plant & Environmental Monitor STARBiE is a compact, intelligent environmental monitoring device designed to help plants stay healthy. It monitors temperature and soil moisture, calculates an overall plant/environment health score, detects abnormal conditions, identifies simple environmental trends, and provides clear alerts and recommendations. It also includes a tilt sensor to detect movement or tipping and uses EEPROM memory to remember tilt events even after power is turned off. A simple one-button interface lets users navigate through the information on the LCD. Key Features: 🌡️ Temperature monitoring 🌱 Soil moisture monitoring ❤️ Environmental health score ⚠️ Alerts and recommendations 📈 Basic trend detection 📐 Tilt detection 💾 EEPROM event memory 🔘 One-button navigation 📟 Real-time LCD display ⚡ Simple, reliable, and low-complexity design STARBiE turns raw sensor data into simple, useful decisions for healthier plants.

## Design

### 2026-10-07 – Today I worked on my Starbie project in Tinkercad. I built and tested the Arduino Uno circuit, connected the 16x2 I2C LCD, temperature sensor, soil moisture sensor, four buttons, and tilt sensor. I al

**5h**

Today I worked on my Starbie project in Tinkercad. I built and tested the Arduino Uno circuit, connected the 16x2 I2C LCD, temperature sensor, soil moisture sensor, four buttons, and tilt sensor. I also wrote and tested the Arduino code and fixed the LCD I2C address and sensor setup. The prototype is now working and can display temperature, soil moisture, system status, and movement detection.

### 2026-10-08 – Today, we worked on STARBiE by simplifying the project and selecting only the most useful features. We finalized temperature and soil-moisture monitoring, health scoring, alerts, recommendations, tren

**14h**

Today, we worked on STARBiE by simplifying the project and selecting only the most useful features. We finalized temperature and soil-moisture monitoring, health scoring, alerts, recommendations, trend detection, tilt detection, EEPROM memory, one-button navigation, and the LCD interface. We also solved the LCD library issue by switching to Adafruit_LiquidCrystal, faced and fixed code/header errors, and tested features separately instead of combining everything at once. We also experimented with adaptive environmental baseline detection, which helped us understand how STARBiE could become more intelligent. Finally, we prepared the simple final code, project thumbnail, project description, and README.md. Overall, today we learned practical debugging, feature testing, hardware integration, code simplification, and how to turn a prototype into a cleaner final project.

### 2026-10-08 – STARBiE uses an Arduino Uno as the main controller. The TMP36 temperature sensor is connected to A0, the soil moisture sensor to A1, the tilt sensor to D7, and the single push button to D3. The 16×2 I

**2h**

STARBiE uses an Arduino Uno as the main controller. The TMP36 temperature sensor is connected to A0, the soil moisture sensor to A1, the tilt sensor to D7, and the single push button to D3. The 16×2 I²C LCD is connected directly to the Arduino's SDA and SCL pins. All components share 5V and GND. The button and tilt sensor use the Arduino's internal pull-up resistors.
